_about: The draft demo video, scene by scene. scripts/demo/record.mjs speaks each line with the macOS voice, records the live app doing the matching steps, and builds demo/AppealPath-demo.mp4. The live read decides which 'correct' line plays: correctMissing if the reader found no deadline, correctFax if the second reader flags the phone as a fax number, correctOk otherwise. sampleFax shows the L04 sample's saved fax mistake, and plays only when the live read didn't already show one. Replace the voice with your own by recording over demo/AppealPath-demo-silent.mp4.

scenes.label: AppealPath
scenes.text: In 2024, insurers on HealthCare.gov denied nearly one in five in-network claims, and fewer than one in a hundred of those denials were appealed. But a denial doesn't always need an appeal. Sometimes the doctor's office just fixes the paperwork. Sometimes you need an urgent review today. AppealPath reads the letter, checks its own work, and points to the right first step. Every letter in this video is fictional.

scenes.label: 1 · Your letter
scenes.text: Here's a simulated phone photo of a fictional denial letter. I add the photo and answer five quick questions: a Marketplace plan, the care already happened, and I live in Missouri.

scenes.label: 2 · Check what we read
scenes.text: The AI reads the letter live and copies what's printed: what was denied, why, the deadline, and who to call. Then a second reader, running on the phone, checks the deadline, the reason and the phone number against the photo.

scenes.label: 2 · Fix what's wrong
scenes.text: And it caught a real mistake: the AI picked the fax number as the phone number. In testing, the AI even said it was one hundred percent sure of a sentence it had copied wrong, so AppealPath never trusts its confidence. I check the number against the letter and fix it before going on.

scenes.label: 2 · Fix what's missing
scenes.text: On this photo the AI couldn't find the deadline, and it won't make one up. So I type it exactly as it's printed on the letter, and AppealPath uses my words.

scenes.label: 2 · Check it against the photo
scenes.text: Show me opens the whole letter with those words highlighted, so checking takes a second. AppealPath never trusts the AI's own confidence: in testing, it said it was one hundred percent sure of a sentence it had copied wrong.

scenes.label: 3 · Appeal
scenes.text: The cardiology visit was denied as out of network, so the next step is an appeal. The deadline is quoted from the letter, never calculated. The app shows why: each rule, in order, up to the one that fit. And there's an appeal letter filled in from the letter's own words.

scenes.label: The mistake that matters
scenes.text: In testing, the AI's most dangerous mistake was picking the fax number as the number to call. This built-in sample is a real reading where it did that. The second reader warns about the number, and if I tap on anyway, the app stops and asks me to compare it with the letter first.

scenes.label: Sample letters
scenes.text: The other samples, also read ahead of time, show the other next steps. This MRI was denied because the office never sent the prior authorization. That's paperwork, so the next step is fix and resubmit, with a script for the call.

scenes.label: Care still ahead
scenes.text: This rehab stay was denied as not medically necessary, a reason that usually leads to an appeal. But the care is still ahead and the doctor says waiting could cause harm, so the rules move it to an urgent review today.

scenes.label: No guessing
scenes.text: Medicare and Medicaid have their own appeal rules, so AppealPath says so the moment you pick one, and doesn't read the letter. A letter with no clear reason gets: call and ask, instead of a guess.

scenes.label: How it decides
scenes.text: Fixed rules pick the next step, each with a source or labeled a design choice. On eighteen fictional test letters, including six written after the reader was frozen, it chose the right step on every image, and the second reader flagged every fax-number mistake. These are fictional letters and simulated photos, so that's a best case.

scenes.label: En español
scenes.text: It also works in Spanish, and the letter's own words aren't translated, so you can check them against the paper.

scenes.label: AppealPath
scenes.text: AppealPath is a prototype, not medical or legal advice, and it doesn't save your photo or answers. It helps people find the right first step after a denial, before the deadline passes.
